pairs.question: What happens to my heart rate right after I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: 20 minutes after quitting, your heart rate drops to a normal level.

pairs.question: How long after quitting does the carbon monoxide level in my blood return to normal?
pairs.answer: 12 to 24 hours after quitting, the carbon monoxide level in your blood drops to normal.

pairs.question: When does my risk of having a heart attack start to decrease after quitting?
pairs.answer: Your risk of having a heart attack begins to drop 2 weeks to 3 months after quitting.

pairs.question: How long does it take for my lung function to start improving after I quit?
pairs.answer: Your lung function begins to improve 2 weeks to 3 months after quitting.

pairs.question: What happens to my risk of coronary heart disease one year after quitting?
pairs.answer: 1 year after quitting, your added risk of coronary heart disease is half that of someone who uses cigarettes or other tobacco products.

pairs.question: How does quitting smoking affect my risk of having a stroke?
pairs.answer: 5 to 15 years after quitting, your risk of having a stroke is reduced to that of someone who does not smoke or use other tobacco products.

pairs.question: What is the impact on my cancer risk 10 years after quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: 10 years after quitting, your risk of dying from lung cancer is about half that of someone who uses cigarettes or other tobacco products.

pairs.answer: 15 years after quitting, your risk of coronary heart disease is the same as that of someone who does not use cigarettes or other tobacco products.
